title: Write things down so new joiners can follow: decisions, product docs and a glossary
summary: When a company grows fast, knowledge lives in a few heads. Write down decisions and how the product works so new people can get up to speed without asking.

beginner: Start a decision log: date, decision, why and who decided.
Write a short page on what the product does and for whom.
Start a glossary of the terms your team uses.
Link everything from one starting page.
Ask the next new joiner what was missing, and add it.
intermediate: Write the decision down first, then announce it with a link.
Agree where each kind of document lives.
Review and prune documents every quarter.
experienced: Make written decisions a norm across product and engineering.
Use short decision records for important technical and product choices.
Measure how long new joiners take to get up to speed.

canDelegateTo.task: Edit pages so they are clear

toolExamples.confluence: Keep the decision log and glossary in one space.
toolExamples.notion: Link all key pages from one team home page.
toolExamples.github: Store decision records next to the code.

definitionOfDone: One starting page links them all
pitfalls: Decisions announced but never written down

sources.title: The importance of a handbook-first approach to communication (GitLab Handbook)
